page: Microsoft Azure DC64ads_cc_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, the system features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 2458 GB disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core performance placing in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is highly polarized; the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10%, and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 4184.42 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth drops to average levels of 117.57 GB/sec and 59.33 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, with Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations scoring in the top 25%. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds are strong for small 135M models but degrade to average for medium 7B models and weak for large 70B models, where text generation drops to 2.74 tokens per second. This profile makes the instance suitable for relational databases, memory-cached data stores, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, while highlighting a performance tradeoff for large-scale AI inference.
